function: Over-the-air federated aggregation with integrated sensing: joint device scheduling, downlink precoding, uplink post-processing, and echo cancellation; the learned element is the trained FL model (pp. 5-9).
system: PS with N=8 antennas, K=20 single-antenna devices, one LoS target; same band for uplink and downlink, 5 GHz, 10 MHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Federated local SGD: logistic regression (MNIST), three-block CNN (CIFAR-10), aggregated over the air; PS design by matching pursuit, SDP/LMI, and eigenvector, not learned (pp. 8-12).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh fading, path-loss exponent 2.5, LoS target echo exponent 4.5; MNIST and CIFAR-10 split 83/17 with Dirichlet non-IID devices (pp. 10, 12).
test_conditions: Test on held-out 17% of MNIST/CIFAR-10; sweeps of error thresholds, downlink SNR, antennas N, target distance, K; stationary target, fixed client distances (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Authors' own heuristics GSOB (greedy) and RSOB (random scheduling), both with optimal beamforming; no-sensing OTA-FEEL and FEEL references; no earlier published design (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Number of selected devices, achievable Cramer-Rao bound, MSE of the estimated sensing channel, test accuracy and test loss (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Order K^2 N^2 with direct SVD, lower with extreme-value decomposition; random, greedy, and exhaustive search compared qualitatively; no runtime (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 10: "The uplink and downlink channels are assumed to experience standard Rayleigh fading"; custom simulator with its own path loss, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "We train on 83% of the dataset and test on the remaining portion" is a held-out split; no unseen scenario, antenna number, or channel is tested, and the target is stationary (p. 13).
q3_support: p. 11: "Random Scheduling with Optimal Beamforming (RSOB)" and "Greedy Scheduling with Optimal Beamforming (GSOB)" are heuristics defined by the authors; no earlier published aggregation design is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "with direct implementation via SVD the complexity of the algorithm scales with" K^2 N^2 for the scheduling and beamforming design.
q5_support: p. 12: "we use logistic regression on the MNIST dataset" and CIFAR-10 are learning-task datasets only; channels are simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included under the over-the-air FL rule: the learned element is the FL model trained across devices, while PS scheduling and beamforming are non-learned (matching pursuit, SDP, eigenvector). Area 7 over 5: the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation with echo cancellation, with the Cramer-Rao bound of sensing as a constraint. q3: GSOB and RSOB are the authors' own heuristics, so the condition of an earlier published aggregation design is not met. q4 counts the order K^2 N^2 of the aggregation design, not the size of the FL model.
